findings: The two six-line stories and titles in every assigned language convey the English story naturally enough for their simple reading level. Minor tense/aspect or explicitly repeated name differences are normal translation choices and were retained.
Mandarin Pinyin n uses a displayed first-tone example nā but a recorded-character request 拿, which is second-tone ná. Fixing the display preserves the existing spoken example.
The Indonesian alphabet currently uses the older written Q name ki. Official EYD V now writes qi but still pronounces it ki.

Official Indonesian EYD V pronounces the written V name ve as fe. Correct the spoken field and resolve exact existing audio or show unavailable/device-voice fallback without mapping to a stale recording.
Korean basic Hangul units and Thai consonant/vowel names are consistent with their stated basic/core coverage. These lists are introductory, not complete phonological curricula.
Japanese じ/ぢ and ず/づ share standard ji/zu readings. Any reverse reading-to-character question must exclude the competing homophone or accept all valid matches.

teachingNotes.note: The 14 consonants and 10 vowels are the basic jamo set; tense/double consonants, compound vowels, syllable-block composition and batchim rules need additional instruction.

The list teaches 21 initials plus y/w spelling letters, six simple finals and four marked tones. It omits compound/nasal finals and a neutral-tone item, so it should be described as introductory rather than complete. The y/w entries are spelling conventions rather than ordinary consonantal initials.
Tone items use 妈/麻/马/骂 as examples, so explain that the tone marks apply to vowels inside the example syllable mā/má/mǎ/mà. Do not imply those recordings are pure isolated ā/á/ǎ/à vowels.

The 58 units contain 44 traditional consonant symbols (including obsolete ฃ and ฅ) and 14 core vowel signs. Teach consonant classes, vowel combinations/length, live/dead syllables and tone marks separately.
Six written tones is the orthographic inventory. Some dialects merge spoken hỏi/ngã, so spelling and a single regional recording should not be described as six universally distinct sounds.
を/ヲ romanized wo preserves the written kana distinction; its common object-particle pronunciation is o. Likewise は/へ have wa/e particle pronunciations in grammar contexts.
안녕히 가세요 is said to the person leaving; when you leave and the other person stays, use 안녕히 계세요.
Selamat tinggal is said by the person leaving to the person staying; selamat jalan is said to the person leaving.
